items.title: Crystal 1.22.3 is released!
items.author: Johannes Müller
items.content:
We are announcing a new Crystal release 1.22.3 with important security patches, regression fixes, and normal bug fixes.

This release includes 14 changes since 1.22.2 by 4 contributors. We thank all the contributors for all the effort put into improving the language! ❤️

Below we list the most significant, security-related changes. For more details, visit the full changelog.

Creating a socket on port higher than 65535 can no longer succeed with a truncated port number (#17848). On some systems, the following snipped would create a socket on port 8080 prior to this patch:

We fixed a couple of bugs in the HTTP message parser which previously accepted some invalid inputs. This could potentially result in a protocol desync with a parser that interprets these invalid message in a different way.

  • control whitespace before field value in HTTP headers (#17903)
  • validates the chunk-line (#17898)
  • validate header (#17902)

These invalid message now always result in an error.

The token in header now always closes the connection, even if there are other values beside it (#17904).

Fix matching after a fragmented delimiter mismatch (#17916).

no longer crashes if the input exceeds max bytesize buffer limit (#17836). This is a regression from 1.22.0.

We have been able to do all of this thanks to the continued support of 84codes and all other sponsors. To maintain and increase the development pace, donations and sponsorships are essential. OpenCollective is available for that.

Reach out to crystal@manas.tech if you’d like to become a direct sponsor or find other ways to support Crystal. We thank you in advance!

items.title: Crystal 1.22.1 is released!
items.author: Johannes Müller
items.content:
We are announcing a new Crystal release 1.22.1 with important security patches and regression fixes, as well as some regular bug fixes.

This release includes 20 changes since 1.22.0 by 7 contributors. We thank all the contributors for all the effort put into improving the language! ❤️

The default configuration for options used outdated options which weakens security assumptions and may compromise encrypted communications.

After some back-and-forth we disabled KernelTLS by default and it’s meant to stay that way.

OpenSSL itself doesn’t enable kernel TLS by default either, because it may cause unexpected behaviour and failures in some scenarios.

We still support kTLS, but you need to opt-in explicitly.
